DECLARED DEPENDENCIES THAT BLOCK — read at 2dfd0fc (every citation anchored to THIS commit, per 12/16's AC-5).

AC-1 — THE FIELD: contract.dependsOn (format v19 — the schema block, the optional-field list and a v19 amendment paragraph recorded in docs/journey-format-spec.md). spawn! validates where a contract ENTERS the journey, refusing by name with zero writes: dependsOn-shape (not an array of non-empty strings) · dependsOn-self · dependsOn-unknown (the target does not exist) · dependsOn-target (not a task id — legs are not targets in this slice). HONEST NOTE ON THE CYCLE GUARD: a cycle cannot be created through spawn at all — every target must already exist and a NEW node has no dependents, so nothing existing can point back at it; the guard is defensive insurance against a future writer path, and the LIVE net is check() (Store.depCycleProblems), tested against a hand-written cycle. check() also names a declared target that has since VANISHED.

AC-2 — THE BLOCKING DERIVATION, ONE PLACE: Store.taskStatus passes the dependency facts into workflowState as INPUT (they arrive from the store, which can see the other nodes, so the projection stays pure over one tail), and the word becomes blocked when the task would otherwise be proposed (queued | active). NO READER CHANGED: a test asserts frontmostReady · lookBack's frontmostReady · advance() all skip the blocked task and propose the dependency-free one. detail() was ALSO fixed to build the same dep-aware projection — its first version read the undeped projection, so a card could have said queued for a task the readers refuse to propose.

AC-3 — THE REASON IS NAMED: the node's blockers carry 'dependency open: <id> (<status>)' and the verdict is waiting-on-dependency — never a bare blocked. (The brief and the card render the blockers already; the declared edge is labelled DECLARED (binding) while a prose-read edge prints 'read from the record (a hint)'.)

AC-4 — SATISFACTION AND THE DEADLOCK RULE: satisfied = done | superseded | cancelled (DEP_SATISFIED_STATUSES, declared once). deferred does NOT satisfy — deferring work does not deliver it, so the dependent stays blocked and the blocker NAMES the deferred target; an ABSENT target does not satisfy either (a NAMED check finding). The derivation terminates on ANY graph: satisfaction reads the target's RAW projection (no deps), so a cycle blocks its members fail-closed instead of recursing.

AC-5 — THE DEPS READ LEARNS THE DISTINCTION: how: 'declared' is read first and is the ONLY kind that can block; the prose/affectedTaskIds edges keep how: 'named-in-record'. A test asserts a prose-only mention NEVER blocks a task (the hint stays a hint).

AC-6 — NO REGRESSION, NO RETRO-BLOCKING: 866 tests green (was 858; +8 for this feature) · typecheck clean · ann check OK · ann verify 0 drifts. The LIVE journey is untouched: 0 of 50 nodes declare dependsOn, and the derived statuses are unchanged (7/17 done, the same nine grills waiting — verified before and after) — the feature is inert until a spawn declares an edge.

POST-SUBMISSION CORRECTION — found by the operator's question: "the blocked by dependency can still perform action?" Answer: IT COULD. Recorded here because the confirm gate had not been decided yet, so the correction lands BEFORE the decision rather than after it.
THE HOLE: the declared-dependency block was enforced on the PROPOSAL path only (frontmostReady · lookBack · advance() filter READY_STATUSES). The EXECUTION seam did not consult it: the frame refuses on packet.readiness, and readiness was inputs + blocking questions ONLY (src/flow/materialize.ts) — so a dependency-blocked task whose grill gate was accepted WOULD have run.
THE FIX, at 080d5d8: readiness gains the third clause — store.openDeps(nodeId) becomes a readiness blocker ("dependency open: <id> (<status>)") — so the frame's not-ready stop refuses run! · the frame · the driver with ZERO writes, and the packet read is honest about why. docs/context-packet-spec.md's readiness definition is amended in place.
PROOF: a frame test asserts the refusal (stop not-ready · phase materialize · the blocker naming the target · the node's events unchanged at [created]); the packet test pins the existing-but-open form ("dependency open: <id> (queued)"). SCOPE OF THE BLOCK, STATED FOR THE RECORD: the block is on EXECUTION (machine work). GATE DECISIONS stay the human's authority — submitting or deciding a gate on a dependency-blocked task is not refused, deliberately: the human may need to reject, cancel or defer it, and a gate decision is not work.
